$comment: The stored audits the test suite reads as fixtures, and why each one is here.
This file exists because of a real failure on 2026-08-25: these directories live
under the gitignored artifacts/ tree, nothing re-derived them when normalization
changed, and nothing detected that they had gone stale. The sas-fernande fixture
was still reporting 78 findings months after collapses that took it to 42, so a
green suite meant nothing for the code those tests claimed to cover.
Two things follow from listing them here. scripts/refresh-fixtures.mjs re-derives
exactly this set with one command, and fixture-freshness.test.ts fails the build
when any of them predates the current normalization code. Adding a new fixture
directory to a test means adding it here as well, or the freshness guard will not
Keep this list curated, not accumulated. A second timestamp for a site already
listed needs a reason of its own written into its 'purpose'.

audits.purpose: Primary small-site fixture: 11 pages, a full severity spread, and a legal page whose findings are diverted. Drives build-input, statistics, observations, the PDF text-integrity check and the report axe audit.
Second sas-fernande scan of the same site, kept for the render-diff evidence path.
Post-milestone-8.5 sas-fernande scan: the only sas-fernande fixture carrying geo findings and reference-stat citations.

Primary multi-page fixture: 20 pages, a site-wide WCAG failure, a high-occurrence single-page finding, and third-party vendor attribution. Drives structure-ranking, diversion, dominant-metric and computeStatistics.
Carries the stored analysis whose real model output the severity-vocabulary guard was written against.
Post-milestone-8.6 haaitza scan: security headers, CrUX field data, structured-data validation, and the rule-translation coverage check.
The scan behind report-feedback-la-corniche: two very large rule families the model ranked 8th and 9th, which is what occurrence weighting exists to correct.
Follow-up La Corniche scan used by the appendix page-union counts.
Largest fixture by finding count. The stress case for annex pagination and Paged.js fragmentation.
Monolingual French site: proves translation clustering is a no-op where a site declares no hreflang.
Re-scan carrying the cookie-consent true negative from milestone 8.6: a real consent platform, zero trackers before consent.

The only fixture where the milestone 8.6 privacy checks fire positively: trackers and a third-party data transfer before consent, alongside broken-internal-link, canonical-target-unreachable, form-error-not-associated and llms-txt-missing. Six rules no other stored scan exercises.

The only post-Lighthouse-upgrade fixture. Lighthouse renamed two dozen audits into an *-insight family, and every other stored scan predates it, so without this one the renamed rules have no coverage at all and the older names it replaced are counted instead.
Pre-fix Domaine Lagnonu scan, kept as the render-diff networkidle regression case (trade-off 31's P0).
Current Domaine Lagnonu scan: trilingual, 43 pages, the reference for translation clustering and template-shape collapse.
